results.claim: The endpoint is https://sunago-matrix.com/mcp
The server reports version 0.3.0
It runs on the official @modelcontextprotocol/sdk
Transport is streamable HTTP
It is stateless: a fresh server per request, so no session is shared between callers
results.evidence: handler.ts builds the server inside the request handler and never reuses it

results.claim: Tokens are verified against the issuer's published keys, with no shared secret
results.evidence: server/oauth.ts uses jose createRemoteJWKSet against the issuer jwks

results.claim: Every call runs as the signed-in user, under row-level security
results.evidence: _client.ts forwards the caller's bearer token to Supabase

results.claim: There is no service-role key anywhere in the MCP surface
results.evidence: no occurrence of service_role in src/lib/mcp

results.claim: 105 tools
31 of them only read
74 can write
Four named prompts: what is waiting on me, project status, log time, ready to invoice
Each tool checks the same feature permission the Matrix interface checks
A refusal names the missing permission so it can be relayed to the user
4 tools read financial data behind finance.view
4 tools write behind finance.create or finance.edit
No tool issues, sends or records payment against an invoice
No tool reads or writes an annual salary
No tool reads or writes a gross hourly rate
No tool reads or writes a national ID
No tool touches bank or card details
Proposals cannot be created or updated through MCP
No tool deletes a contract
No tool deletes an employee
The derived cost per hour is returned per named employee by reports_get, behind reports.view
results.evidence: reports.ts selects cost_price_per_hour and returns cost_per_hour on each row

results.claim: The derived cost per hour is returned per named employee by timelog_recalculate_cost, behind time.approve
results.evidence: timelog.ts builds perEmployee rows carrying rate, after requiring time.approve

results.claim: timelog_recalculate_cost previews by default and only writes when told to
hr_update_employee can grant or remove workspace administrator rights, behind hr.edit
results.evidence: hr.ts declares is_admin on the input schema and gates on hr.edit

results.claim: hr_get_employees returns no salary, cost rate or national ID
results.evidence: hr.ts selects an explicit column list containing none of them

results.claim: Roles are validated against the workspace's own list, read at call time
results.evidence: hr.ts resolveWorkspaceRole reads workspaceRoles and refuses anything not in it

results.claim: 5 deletes are soft: 30 days in the recycle bin, and admin only
results.evidence: each says so in its own description, and calls requireAdmin

results.claim: 13 deletes are permanent
10 tools require a human-supplied confirmation phrase
notifications_delete asks for a phrase only when several are deleted at once
12 tools are restricted to workspace admins
results.evidence: requireAdmin in the handler or in the factory that builds it

results.claim: Every write is recorded with the tool, the caller and the resolved arguments
results.evidence: _reporting.ts defineTool audits after resolveReferences has run

results.claim: Reads are not recorded, and not rate limited
results.evidence: _reporting.ts audits and meters only when isWrite

results.claim: Writes are limited to 120 per minute per user
Every tool runs through that wrapper, so none can ship without an audit row
results.evidence: every module under tools/ imports defineTool from ./_reporting

results.claim: Reference arguments accept a name as readily as a UUID, resolved in the wrapper
results.evidence: _resolve.ts FIELD_KINDS, applied by defineTool before any handler sees the input

results.claim: An ambiguous name returns every candidate rather than picking one
results.evidence: _resolve.ts raises rather than choosing when more than one row matches
